speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits or stool color related to your abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Those symptoms are concerning for a malignancy or chronic infection. Have you noticed any blood in your stool or black, tarry stools? Additionally, do you have a known history of gastric ulcers or a family history of stomach cancer?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, LDH.
REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis, CT_Chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal; Lactate Dehydrogenase: Elevated; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: Not provided; CT Chest and Abdomen: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma).

The combination of B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and massively enlarged lymph nodes in multiple regions (cervical, mediastinal, axillary) with elevated LDH strongly suggests a lymphoproliferative disorder rather than a primary gastrointestinal malignancy or infection. I will proceed with a tissue biopsy for definitive confirmation.
